text:
Trevor Zegras's season has turned sour in the last few weeks. He sat for 10 minutes in a loss early this month after a misconduct for tapping his stick at a referee, which The New York Times and others reported left Rick Tocchet unhappy. He's gone pointless in his last four games, and our numbers say the chances have thinned out too.

The season-long picture is mixed. Four goals on 6.3 expected (the quality of his chances) is a finishing gap that usually closes, and he's shooting 8.9% against a talent range near 13.5%. The worrying number is five on five: the Flyers have had only 37.6% of the expected goals with him on the ice, 8.4 points worse than when he sits.

That's a long way from last season, when Evolving-Hockey had him driving play in the 94th percentile among forwards. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 55% of his entries. Watch the line Tocchet tried with Porter Martone and Matvei Michkov; if the rush game comes back, the rest probably follows.
headline: Zegras is in a rough patch
